flags: Periods, the judgement calls: where a card says only that a classical word’s computing sense is “a modern extension” or “applied to” it and cites no modern source, I could not tell whether the usage is ours or established, so I chose the later period, ours: cōdex “code”, conjungō “merge”, mendum “bug”, ēmendō “debug”. Also marked ours on the card’s wording alone: programmātūra computātrālis (no label of its own) and lingua programmātiōnis / lingua programmandī (“descriptive phrases”). Make them modern if they are established usage.

programmātrīx: the card says only “a transparent feminine counterpart”, without a source. Traupman 261 gives it (programmer: programmātor, -tōris m. (-trīx, -trīcis f.)), so I marked it modern; the citation could be added.

partēs programmātiōnis: the “reported lexical proposal” is Traupman’s (p. 262, software: partēs, -ium f. pl. programmātiōnis), which the card does not cite. Marked modern. Traupman 261 gives hardware as apparātus computātrālis, not the card’s apparātūra.
Traupman gives programma on p. 261; p. 262 has programma compōnere. The card cites 262 for both, and I kept its citation.

program (verb): programmō leads, as the Programming card (entry-42) gives it, and programma compōnere (Traupman 262) is an alternative. Libellus III uses programma compōnere, and its gloss gives that form, so you may prefer it as the lead, as with vestis nocturna for pyjamas.
telephone: the card gives no source for tēlephōnum (the sources line says so). Traupman 38 has tēlephōnum, -ī n.

recōgnitiō (code review): the card marks the o long after Lewis’s Elementary (re-cōgnitiō); Lewis & Short (rĕcognĭtĭo) leaves it unmarked, and the quantity-authorities ruling sends hidden quantities to Bennett. The short-before-gn ruling may bear on it, and entry-312 (sermo) writes cognātus with a short o. The note follows the card.

Suspected macron errors, copied as printed: entry-139 “Numerōs inspicere debeō.” (Lewis & Short dēbĕo; the house writes īnspicere, as in four other entries and Libellus III’s īnspexit) and entry-140 “Catalogum inspiciam.” (→ īnspiciam). Entry-138 quotes the earlier proposals “reproducere vitium” and “gradūs ad vitium reproducendum” without macrons; I kept them as quotations in the comment, unmarked as Latin, as the card has them.
entry-53 (Technical noun relationships) is a usage note, not a word. I folded it into code-review (its first example) as part of the comment and in replaces. It might be better as a usage ruling.

Merges within the batch: defect (vitium) is an alternative in bug, since entry-137 keeps mendum as the everyday “bug”. “Report a bug” is in bug-report (noun and verb). “Fix a bug / an error” and the correction nouns are in debug. Quality testing (probātiō quālitātis) is in testing, and QA is its own record, since the card says they are not synonyms. Kinds of testing and the parts of a test case have records of their own.

Likely overlaps with other batches: telephone and screen with sermo entry-240 (tēlephōnum sonat; in quadrō appāruit), which may produce its own telephone or phone record; project (opus) with sermo entry-170 (opus, a job). “Key” itself (clāvis) is in domus entry-89, so I made no key record; clāvis is explained inside api-key. project and plan are general words that I kept in computatra, the card’s category.

Senses were added to headwords that other categories may also use: bug (software), code and script and program (computing), merge and commit (version control), screen (of a device), plan (of action), permission (access right).
audience is left at the default (child), although these are adult words: the cards do not say.
